evidence.text:
## Which code paths serve 2 RTX, local experts, no Sparks

The answer depends on the attention placement, so it is settled first.

| Placement | How it is selected | DSA index cache served | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context` (token-split MLA) | **auto on two GPUs**; fails closed if the image lacks its programs | compact (per-sequence open-pool tails) | `rust/crates/cuteafd-loader/src/placement/families/glm5_flash.rs:57-75` ("Auto is `context` on two GPUs"); `rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/families/glm5_flash/mod.rs:1383-1390` (`Context => Compact`) |
| `heads` (head split) | explicit `ATTENTION_PLACEMENT=heads` | keys (per-token key, gate row) | same `mod.rs:1388` (`Heads if split => Keys`); `python/tools/aot/export_b12x_dsv4_aot.py:441` ("The head split keeps the per-token index keys") |
| `layers` | explicit only | whatever was requested; the launcher passes keys on a split | `mod.rs:1389`; `scripts/launch/run-family.sh:2018-2030` |

- The v3 2-RTX release card is `benchmarks/glm5_flash/2026-10-18-…-2rtx-glm53f-exl3-max/report.json`. It reads "2 RTX (head split) · experts on the coordinator".
- Both index-cache variants were audited below. The `layers` placement uses the same programs as `heads` and was not audited separately.

findings.question: Does CuteAFD v3.0.1 keep all 512 selected index pools (the vLLM-engine issue D1 dropped column 511)?
findings.statement: From source: all 512 selected pools are expanded, plus the open tail pool, into a 2,112-slot row on every path read, and rows of exactly 512 pools take the dense branch; audit verdict: handled correctly. Not audited: whether the b12x top-k kernel's selected set is exact.
findings.quantity: audit verdict from reading the source

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text: | **D1**: keeps 511 of 512 selected pools (drops column 511) | **handled correctly**: all 512 selected pools are expanded, plus the open tail pool, into a 2,112-slot row | `si:b12x/integration/cuteafd/_glmf_kernels.py:1058-1077` (`if j < Int64(self.pools)` … `lengths[row] = Int32(filled + tail)`); `engine.rs:89-90` (`SPARSE_TOPK = 2112`, "2048 + 3") |

**CuteAFD counterpart.**
- `engine.rs:24-26`: "The indexer selects every earlier token up to 2051 tokens; past that the top 512 pools (glmf_index_topk) expand to tokens plus the open tail pool."
- Selection width: `engine.rs:89-90` defines `SPARSE_TOPK: usize = 2112`, documented as "2048 + 3, padded to 64". The geometry is `si:…/_common.py:359-361`: `sparse_topk = ceil((index_topk + index_kpool - 1) / 64) * 64`.
- Heads placement, and prefill under every placement: `engine.rs:4689-4704` runs `index_topk_{mode}_{cap}` into `pools`, then `index_expand`.
- `si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:1003-1077` (`GlmfIndexExpand`):
  - rows with `count <= dense_limit` (2,051) select every earlier token (`:1047`);
  - longer rows loop `j < self.pools` (512) and expand each pool to its four record slots (`:1058-1068`);
  - then the open tail pool `count - tail_start` (0-3 tokens) is appended after `filled = pools * kpool` (`:1070-1075`);
  - `lengths = filled + tail` (`:1077`).
  - No column is discarded, so output order cannot matter.
- Context decode (the 2-GPU default): `engine/context.rs:15-19` describes "merge into the global top-512 by (score desc, logical asc)".
  - `si:…/context_split.py:236-280` (`_CandidateMerge`): "A + reverse(B) is bitonic … Its first compare-exchange retains exactly the global best K pairs" (`:237-238`), with K = 512.
  - Each GPU then expands its share in `si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:1080-1172` (`GlmfIndexExpandOwned`): `picked = local_lengths * 4` plus the tail on its owner (`:1155-1172`). "Shard unions equal the full selection."
- The exactly-512-pools case: 512 complete pools means 2,048-2,051 tokens, which is at or below `dense_limit` = 2,051. Those rows take the dense branch and select every token.

**Verdict: handled correctly.** The 512-pool selection is kept whole on every path read. The tail tokens have their own columns.

**Not audited.** Whether the b12x top-k kernel's selected *set* is exact: the GLM index top-k is `dsv4_indexer._TopK`, called from `si:…/glm_indexer.py`. That is outside D1. The vLLM investigation measured the set exact apart from ties on its own b12x kernels, and this audit did not compare CuteAFD's kernel revision with those.

findings.question: Does CuteAFD v3.0.1 have a counterpart of the vLLM-engine issue D2 (index tail ring written without positions)?
findings.statement: From source: there is no tail ring or generic mapping fallback; every slot is addressed from the row's own position and its sequence's pages, and a position outside them is an error. Audit verdict: not applicable (different design).
findings.quantity: audit verdict from reading the source

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text: | **D2**: tail ring written without positions (null block, foreign blocks) | **not applicable (different design)**: there is no tail-ring view or generic mapping fallback; every slot comes from the row's own position | `engine.rs:653-665` (`record`, `pool_slot` from `position`), `engine.rs:3226-3240` (`rows()` per position); compact tails take `positions`/`seq_first`/`kda_slots` (`engine.rs:4615-4622`) |

**CuteAFD counterpart.** CuteAFD has no tail ring and no per-group block-table mapping.
- **Keys cache** (heads):
  - Every token's key and gate row is stored at the row's own MLA record slot (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:911-918`, "stored … at `token_keys[slots[row]]` (negative slots skip)").
  - Pools read it back by record slot (`:966`).
- **Compact cache** (context, one GPU):
  - The open pool's at most three rows live in a per-sequence tail inside the sequence's KDA slot region (`engine.rs:20-23`; `TAIL_BYTES` at `engine.rs:176-179`).
  - The producer receives `positions`, `kda_slots` and `seq_first` explicitly (`engine.rs:4615-4622`; kernel `si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:1293-1476`).
- **Slot addressing** is computed on the host from the row's position and its own sequence's pages:
  - `engine.rs:653-656`: `record(position)` = `pages[position / 64] * 64 + position % 64`.
  - `engine.rs:659-665`: `pool_slot(position)` is -1 unless `position % 4 == 3`.
  - `engine.rs:3226-3240`: `rows()` pushes `positions`, `kv_slots`, `pool_slots`, `kda_slots`, `seq_first` and `cache_lengths = (position + 1) / 4` per row.
  - A position outside the sequence's pages is an error (`.context("position past the sequence's pages")`), not a fallback.

**Verdict: not applicable (different design).** The function the vLLM tail ring serves is carried out by position-addressed, per-sequence storage.
- In speculative steps, the compact tails stay unchanged during verify.
- `GlmfIndexTailCommit` (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:1479-1545`) rebuilds them from the kept rows.

findings.question: Are router logits computed in FP32 in CuteAFD v3.0.1 (the vLLM-engine issue D3 computed them in BF16 on SM12x)?
findings.statement: From source: BF16 operands, FP32 accumulation and an FP32 store on both GEMM routes, with bias and selection in FP32; `moe_router_dtype` is not read, so FP32 is unconditional. Audit verdict: handled correctly; no numerical comparison was run.

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text: | **D3**: router logits computed in bf16 on SM12x | **handled correctly**: BF16 operands, FP32 accumulation and an FP32 store on both GEMM routes; the bias is added and selection runs in FP32 | `si:…/glmf.py:1249` (`RoutedBf16Projection(e, h, out_dtype=cutlass.Float32)`); `si:b12x/gemm/bf16_gemv/_skinny.py:201`, `si:…/_prefill.py:408`; `native/shared/cuda/expert_router.cu:80,85,103` |

**CuteAFD counterpart.**
- Call site: `engine.rs:4779-4787` (`moe_front`), and `engine.rs:2484-2492` for the second rank under a split.
  - `router_scores` writes `router_logits`, which is `experts * 4` bytes per row (FP32).
  - `router_select(…, routed_scale, true /* sigmoid */, …)` follows.
- Program: `si:…/glmf.py:1246-1270`.
  - `_RouterScores` uses `RoutedBf16Projection(e, h, out_dtype=cutlass.Float32)` (`:1249`).
  - Its doc: "FP32 router logits `x @ gate^T` (BF16 operands, FP32 accumulation)" (`:1260`).
- Both routes keep FP32 to the store:
  - Skinny GEMV, up to 160 rows for N = 288: `si:b12x/gemm/bf16_gemv/_skinny.py:191-203`. The FP32 `total` is converted to `out_dtype` (Float32) and stored (`:201`).
  - TMA tensor-core GEMM above 160 rows: `si:…/_prefill.py:213-214` accepts a Float32 output, and `:408` stores `acc[index].to(output.element_type)` from FP32 accumulators.
- Selection: `native/shared/cuda/expert_router.cu:73-113`, `select_fast_kernel<true,true>` (dispatched at `:296`).
  - FP32 sigmoid of the FP32 logit (`:80`).
  - FP32 `score + e_score_correction_bias` for ranking (`:85`).
  - The weight is the unbiased sigmoid score read back from memory (`:103`), normalised and scaled by `routed_scaling_factor` (`:111`).
- Operand dtypes:
  - `weights.rs:588-589` loads `mlp.gate.weight` as stored and `e_score_correction_bias` widened to FP32.
  - The local K3.25 headers show `mlp.gate.weight` BF16 `[288, 4096]` and `e_score_correction_bias` F32 `[288]`, so the GEMM operands are the checkpoint's own BF16.
- CuteAFD does not read `moe_router_dtype` (no reference in `rust/` or `python/` for this family). The FP32 path is unconditional.

**Verdict: handled correctly.** The computation is the upstream fp32-output form: BF16 operands, FP32 accumulation, FP32 logits. Only the summation order differs from `torch.mm`. This verdict is from source; no numerical comparison was run.

findings.question: Does the routed SwiGLU limit reach CuteAFD v3.0.1's compiled expert kernels (the vLLM-engine issue D4 did not pass it)?
findings.statement: From source, for local EXL3 routed experts: the limit is compiled at 10 and checked at startup (a package without it is refused); shared and dense MLPs also clamp at 10. Audit verdict: handled correctly. Not read: the clamp inside b12x mixed_trellis; whether activations reach 10 was not measured.
findings.quantity: audit verdict from reading the source

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text: | **D4**: routed SwiGLU limit not passed | **handled correctly** for local EXL3 routed experts: compiled at 10, and the runtime refuses a package without it. Shared and dense MLPs are also clamped at 10 | `python/tools/aot/package_exl3_aot.py:238-242`; `python/tools/aot/export_b12x_exl3_aot.py:214`; `rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/shared/experts/exl3/execution.rs:551`; `si:…/glmf.py:1133` |

**CuteAFD counterpart: local EXL3 routed experts on RTX.**
- **Export.**
  - `python/tools/aot/package_exl3_aot.py:236-242`: `SWIGLU_LIMITS = {'glm': None, 'qwen4': None}` and `swiglu_limit(geometry)` returns `SWIGLU_LIMITS.get(geometry, 10.0)`. The GLM 5.3 Flash geometry is `glmf` (`rust/crates/cuteafd-core/src/expert_geometry.rs:242`), so it gets 10.0.
  - `python/tools/aot/export_b12x_exl3_aot.py:117` defaults `swiglu_limit=10.0`, and `:214` passes `swiglu_limit=swiglu_limit` into the options of `compile_mixed_trellis` (`:230`). That is the same b12x entry point the vLLM fix patched.
  - The manifest records it (`:281`).
- **Runtime guard.**
  - `rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/shared/experts/exl3/execution.rs:546-553`, in `with_modules`, the constructor every EXL3 execution goes through, including local RTX `shared/experts/local.rs:314` and TP2 `shared/experts/rtx/exl3.rs:445`.
  - It requires `meta.swiglu_limit == cuteafd_core::expert_geometry().swiglu_limit()`, or startup fails with "EXL3 export/residency geometry mismatch".
  - The expected value is `expert_geometry.rs:251-253`: `Some(10.0)` for every shape except GLM 5, MiMo and Qwen 4.
  - The manifest field is `Option<f32>` (`execution.rs:179`), so a package without the key reads as `None` and is refused.
  - The same key is part of the reduction-plan signature (`execution.rs:118`).
- **Shared expert and dense MLPs.**
  - `si:…/glmf.py:1133`: `GlmSwiGLU(self.i, limit=g.swiglu_limit)`, used by the BF16, FP8 and W8 variants (`:1124-1190`).
  - `si:…/_glm_kernels.py:551-553`: `gate = fmin(gate, limit)`; `up = fmax(fmin(up, limit), -limit)`.
  - The geometry is `si:…/_common.py:315`, `swiglu_limit: float = 10.0`.
  - The head-split half geometry keeps it (`python/tools/aot/export_b12x_dsv4_aot.py:711-713` changes heads and intermediates only).

**Verdict: handled correctly.** The limit reaches the compiled routed-expert kernels, and the runtime enforces it.

**Not read.** The clamp's implementation inside b12x `mixed_trellis`. Whether activations reach 10 was not measured here; it was not measured in the vLLM investigation either.

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text: | **D5**: workspace not locked after graph capture | **not applicable (different design)**: step workspaces are fixed-capacity, allocated before capture, and never replaced. No resize path was found (not exhaustive, see detail) | `engine.rs:1834` ("Allocate fixed workspaces before measuring the graph executables"), `engine.rs:3085-3091`, `engine.rs:3062-3063` |

**CuteAFD counterpart.**
- Decode is captured per segment (`engine.rs:4221-4290`). Replay assumes "the graph's pointers are persistent engine buffers of that rank" (`:4234`).
- The capture itself states: "capture records this stream's launches; nothing in a segment synchronizes the host or allocates" (`:4250-4251`).
- The decode workspace:
  - is allocated once at the configured decode capacity, only when absent (`engine.rs:3080-3093`, `if cell.borrow().is_none()`);
  - is allocated before startup capture (`engine.rs:1833-1836`, "Allocate fixed workspaces before measuring the graph executables' physical memory");
  - cannot be installed a second time (`engine.rs:3056-3066`, "step workspaces already allocated").
- `prepare_serving_workspaces` (`engine.rs:1805-1813`) allocates the decode workspaces, prefill lanes and drafter workspace before readiness.
- Prefill lanes can only be appended (`engine.rs:3097-3115`), and prefill runs eagerly.
- The DFlash2 drafter is eager: "Eager per-round launch" (`rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/families/glm5/dflash.rs:966-967`). Its workspace is recreated only if smaller than the step (`:951-955`), and it is always sized at `max_sequences`.

**Verdict: not applicable (different design).** There is no growable shared workspace, so there is nothing to lock. Within `glm5_flash/engine.rs` and the drafter, no path reallocates a buffer that a captured graph references.

**Limit of this audit.** Not every shared component was audited for lazily grown device buffers referenced inside decode segments: the EXL3 shared arenas, peer-exchange buffers and token I/O.

findings.question: Can stale warm-up block ids reach CuteAFD v3.0.1's tables (the vLLM-engine issue D6)?
findings.statement: From source: tables are rebuilt from the placement every step, padding and warm-up rows carry -1 slots that the writers skip, and per-sequence state is reset or restored before first use. Audit verdict: not applicable (different design).
findings.quantity: audit verdict from reading the source

scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)

evidence.text: | **D6**: stale warm-up tail block ids | **not applicable (different design)**: tables are rebuilt from the placement every step; padding and warm-up rows carry -1 slots; a KDA/tail slot is zeroed before a sequence's first step | `rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/shared/decode_graph.rs:63-65`; `engine.rs:3582-3592`; `engine.rs:2758-2760`, `2860-2868` |

**CuteAFD counterpart.**
- There is no persistent per-runner-row block table. Each step's tables are built on the host from the sequences' placements and uploaded before the step (`engine.rs:3582-3592`, `put_tables`). Under context, they are uploaded "after both streams drained" (`engine/context.rs:32-33`).
- Padding rows, and the all-masked startup graph captures (`engine.rs:1569-1575`, `startup_tables`), use `masked_row` (`rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/shared/decode_graph.rs:63-65`):
  - `position: -1, kv_slot: -1, pool_slot: -1, state_slot: -1`.
  - The writers skip negative slots (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:911-912`; pool keys only for `pool >= 0`, `:965`, `:1381`).
  - `GlmfIndexExpand` gives a negative position an empty selection (`count <= dense_limit` with count 0).
- A new sequence's KDA state and compact tails are zeroed before its first step: `start()` (`engine.rs:2758-2760`) calls `reset_slot` (`:2860-2868`), from `prefill_step` when `start == 0` (`engine.rs:3297-3298`).
- A prefix restore copies a captured mark, including the tails, into the sequence's own slot (`prefix.rs:413-423`).

**Verdict: not applicable (different design).** No warm-up state is carried in slot tables, and every per-sequence state region is reset or restored before use.

- `GlmfPoolKeys` (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:922-1000`): "The pool is the row's own token and the three before it (record slots `slots[row] - 3 .. slots[row]`: a pool never crosses a 64-row page)".
- `first = slots[token] - 3` (`:966`). Members come from `token_keys` at the sequence's own record slots, not from neighbouring batch rows.
- Those keys persist from the earlier chunk or step (`GlmfIndexPost`, `:908-919`), and the post runs before the pool in the same program (`si:…/glmf.py:1362-1363`).
- Record slots are per-sequence (`engine.rs:653-656`). A 4-aligned pool lies in one 64-row page, so its four slots are contiguous.

**Compact cache (context, one GPU).**
- `GlmfPoolKeysTail` (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:1293-1476`): "the ones in this step from its key | gate rows …, the ones before it from the tail of its sequence's KDA slot" (`:1296-1301`).
- `held = start % 4` (`:1375`). For each member, `before = at < first` (the sequence's first step row) selects `tail + TAIL_HEADER + t * KEY_ROW_BYTES` (`:1385-1391`).
- Other sequences' rows are never read, because the boundary is `seq_first`, not the batch.

**Prefix cache.**
- A restore point can be any `kda_len` (`prefix.rs:32-35`, exact frontiers).
- A fork copies a partial tail unit's rows, including token keys in keys mode, and its complete pools (`prefix.rs:439-463`; header `:8-9`).
- Compact tails travel in the KDA mark (`prefix.rs:11-16`).

**Verdict: handled correctly.** Unaligned chunk starts can occur: restores at any length, and prefill after decode. Each straddling pool has a defined source: the sequence's own stored keys, or its own tail.

findings.question: Do CuteAFD v3.0.1's router weights or logits depend on batch size (the vLLM observation E1)?
findings.statement: From source: the E1 mechanism ((s+b)−b rebuild above 1,024 rows) does not apply, since the weight is read from the stored unbiased score and no branch depends on the row count. Whether logits are bit-identical across the 160/161-row GEMV/GEMM route switch could not be determined from source.

findings.replication: the route-switch part was measured afterwards on one GPU: E1-route-logits, E1-route-selection (2026-10-26-e1-router-route)

evidence.text: | **E1**: router weights vary with batch size (fp32 `(s+b)−b` rebuild above 1,024 rows) | **not applicable (different design)** for that mechanism. **Cannot determine** whether router *logits* are bitwise identical across the GEMV/GEMM switch at 160/161 rows | `native/shared/cuda/expert_router.cu:103` (weight read from the unbiased score); `si:…/_skinny.py:232,456` (switch at 160 rows) |

**CuteAFD counterpart.**
- **Selection and weights:** `native/shared/cuda/expert_router.cu:73-113`. One CTA of 512 threads per row. The weight takes `selected[rank]=scores[row*experts+i]` (`:103`), the stored unbiased sigmoid score, not a rebuilt one. No branch depends on the row count.
- **Logits:** `RoutedBf16Projection.__call__` switches route on the live row count (`si:…/_skinny.py:453-465`). For N = 288 the skinny GEMV serves up to 160 rows (`skinny_max_rows`, `:225-232`) and the TMA tensor-core GEMM serves more.
  - Decode and verify steps of 64 or 128 rows fall on the skinny side. Prefill chunks above 160 rows fall on the TMA side.
  - The two routes use different FP32 summation orders. The source makes no bit-equality claim across them; it makes one only within the TMA tile variants (`:288-291`) and within skinny row tiles (`:235-238`).
  - `engine.rs:4767-4771` (`moe_front` doc) runs the router scores over each packed sequence's own rows; `docs/models/glm5_flash.md:123-126` gives the reason: "as its own pass would". `docs/models/glm5_flash.md:395-397` states that batch-invariant prefill and verify are deferred.

**Verdict.**
- The E1 mechanism ((s+b)−b above 1,024 rows): **not applicable (different design)**.
- Router-logit bit equality across the 160/161-row route switch: **cannot determine from source**.
- Measured afterwards on one GPU: see `results/2026-10-26-e1-router-route/` in this repository.

findings.question: Which of CuteAFD v3.0.1's MLP clamps and related keys are read from the checkpoint's config.json?
findings.statement: From source: routed experts, shared expert and dense MLPs clamp at 10 from compiled constants, none reads `swiglu_limit` from config.json, and no equality check was found, so a checkpoint declaring another value would not be detected (the local K3.25 declares 10.0). `routed_scaling_factor`, `index_topk` and `index_kpool` are read; `moe_router_dtype` is not.
findings.quantity: which consumers read swiglu_limit and related keys from config.json

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652
scope.checkpoint: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (config.json and safetensors headers only)
scope.items: the code paths named in the question
scope.path: source reading; no behaviour measured, released image not inspected

evidence.text:
| Consumer | Clamp applied | Source of the value | Reads `config.json`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routed experts, local EXL3 (RTX, TP1 or TP2) | 10 | EXL3 export default per geometry (`package_exl3_aot.py:238-242`; `export_b12x_exl3_aot.py:117,214`), checked against the expert-shape constant (`expert_geometry.rs:251-253`; `exl3/execution.rs:551`) | No |
| Shared expert (I = 2048) and dense MLPs (layers 0-2, I = 12288) | 10: gate ≤ 10, up ∈ [−10, 10] | `si:…/_common.py:315` → `glmf.py:1133` → `_glm_kernels.py:551-553`, baked at AOT export | No |
| DFlash2 drafter | none; it has no experts | dense Qwen3-style MLP (local `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2/config.json`: `model_type` qwen3, `intermediate_size` 12288, no `swiglu_limit`); `native/families/glm5/cuda/glm_dflash.cu:154-160` is an unclamped `silu(g)*u` | n/a (its config has no such key) |

- `config.json`'s `swiglu_limit` is parsed into `GlmNextConfig.swiglu_limit` (`rust/crates/cuteafd-loader/src/families/glm5_flash/config.rs:110`, `unwrap_or(0.0)`). It is printed in plan notes (`rust/crates/cuteafd-loader/src/plan/families/glm.rs:312-315`).
- No GLM Flash engine code that consumes it, and no check that it equals the compiled 10, was found: `grep '\.swiglu_limit'` in `rust/` finds only the EXL3 and FP8 guards and test fixtures.
- The local K3.25 checkpoint carries `swiglu_limit: 10.0`, so compiled and declared values agree for this checkpoint. A checkpoint declaring another value would not be detected.

Related keys:
- `routed_scaling_factor` is read (`config.rs:109`) and used as the selection scale (`engine.rs:4787`).
- `scoring_func`, `n_group` and `norm_topk_prob` are validated: an `ensure!` requires normalized sigmoid with no groups (`config.rs:89-91`).
- `moe_router_dtype` (`"float32"` in the checkpoint) is not read; FP32 logits are unconditional (D3).
- `e_score_correction_bias` is loaded as FP32 (`weights.rs:589`).
- `index_topk` (2048) and `index_kpool` (4) are read (`config.rs:120-121`). The programs are compiled for the same constants (`si:…/_common.py:305-306`), and the pool kernels refuse any `kpool != 4` (`si:…/_glmf_kernels.py:937`, `:1316`, `:1494`).

evidence.text:

  `enable_thinking:false` (reasoning arrives in content).

evidence.text:
- The scheduling explanation is **supported** (`t2.py`). vLLM decode windows overlap other streams'
  prefill by a median 40-81%, CuteAFD's by 0-51%. Streams whose window overlaps less than 5% decode at
  the same speed on both engines:

  | Cell | vLLM clean stream (tok/s) | CuteAFD clean stream (tok/s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 32K code c16 | 45.0 | 45.6 |
  | 32K prose c8 | 50.4 | 49.7 |
  | 128K code c4 | 95.4 | 90.5 |
  | 128K prose c4 | 72.6 | 76.6 |

  So the 1.5-4x is prefill-first vs interleaved scheduling. It trades against vLLM's earlier first

findings.question: Where does the vLLM fork v0.9.2's run-to-run variation on the fidelity set start?
findings.statement: Every vLLM capture ran alone with identical prefill chunking; generated rows bit-equal between the two same-launch runs: 100% in the 20 one-step windows, 46% in the 14 two-step windows and 0% in windows of 4, 8 and 10 prefill steps, and within two-step windows every row of the first 2,045-token chunk is bit-equal (audit).

scope.engine: vLLM fork v0.9.2 release image
scope.items: fidelity set (P-B), 64 windows

findings.replication: consistent with the run's verification of 4 windows (RESULTS-Q.md:11-14)

evidence.text:
**I1. vLLM's run-to-run variation was attributed to another cause, and its size was understated.**
- *Claim.* `RESULTS-Q.md:45-46` says vLLM repeats differ slightly ("P-B KL ±0.0006, Q2 floor KL 0.0047"),
  "as expected with continuous batching and speculation on".
- *Evidence: no batching.* Every vLLM capture ran alone. `vllm-v092-dumps/runs/v1-r{1,2}/{pa,pb,q2}/capture-manifest.json`
  has `steps_with_other_requests = 0` for all 25 + 64 + 18 (r1) and 25 + 64 + 6 (r2) windows. Chunking is
  identical between the two runs (64/64 windows have the same `chunk_lens`), and `cached_tokens` is 0.
- *Evidence: where the variation starts.* `pb3.py` splits windows by number of prefill steps:

  | Prefill steps | Windows | Gen rows bit-equal between V1 and V1r | Mean \|ΔKL\| per gen row |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 20 | 100% | 0 |
  | 2 | 14 | 46% | 0.011 |
  | 4 | 12 | 0% | 0.008 |
  | 8 | 12 | 0% | 0.024 |
  | 10 | 6 | 0% | 0.022 |

  Inside 2-step windows, rows of the first 2,045-token chunk are 100% bit-equal and rows of the second
  chunk are 2-67% bit-equal (`a04`, `d01`, `d04`, `c03`). This matches the earlier finding in
  `contrib/local-inference-evals/LEDGER.md:768-800` (amendments 22ax-22az): identical solo prefills
  diverge from the layer-3 indexer top-k at token 2,051, the first position where sparse selection
  applies.

1. **vLLM run-to-run variation: cause.** It is not batching or speculation: every vLLM capture ran alone.
   Rows inside the first 2,045-token prefill chunk are bit-identical between the two vLLM runs; rows beyond it almost
   never are (verified: e00 512/512 and d01 419/419 identical inside; a08 and b00 0/512 beyond). Multi-chunk prefill is
   not run-to-run deterministic on this stack (consistent with the earlier indexer top-k ordering finding).

scope.items: Block T: 1,008 requests per engine (prose, code, json and reasoning prompts; 1K, 8K, 32K, 128K inputs; 1-16 streams; 3 replicates), 1,024 output tokens, thinking on, temperature 1.0

evidence.text:
**I2. The claim of identical inputs does not hold for two Block T details.**
- *Nonces differ between engines.* `block_t.py:20` says requests "pair across engines". The nonce salt is
  `label:time_ns` (`block_t.py:213`), so 0 of 1,008 paired requests share a nonce: every prompt differs
  in its first line between engines. Seeds still pair, but at temperature 1.0 with two different samplers
  they do not pair the outputs either.
- *128K code prompts differ by 24 tokens.* All 24 C1 requests at 128K code report 131,096 / 131,095
  prompt tokens against the expected 131,072 / 131,071; vLLM matches the expectation. Those prompts
  (vLLM source) contain literal `<think>` once and `</think>` 11 times (checked in
  `stage0/prompts/T/code/128k/p*.json`). vLLM's chat path tokenizes them as special tokens; CuteAFD
  tokenizes them as text. So A2's "thinking on gives both engines the same prompt"
  (`PROTOCOL-DRAFT.md:168-172`) does not hold for those cells: vLLM's model sees 11 end-of-thinking
  control tokens inside the user turn.
- *Impact.* Negligible for throughput. It is a stack difference: control-token strings in user text are parsed as control
  tokens on vLLM.

findings.question: Besides FP8 projections, FP8 head and KDA FP8, how else do CuteAFD v3.0.1's and the vLLM fork v0.9.2's arithmetic differ, and is F1's KDA arm a single-factor test?
findings.statement: Read from source and logs, not measured: the engines also differ in DSA index-key format (CuteAFD BF16, vLLM FP8), attention placement (token split vs whole layers per GPU), KDA split path, prefill chunk geometry, BF16 logits in vLLM, and CuteAFD's W8A8 prefill GEMMs. F1's KDA arm (GLM5_FLASH_KDA_FP8=off) also removes KDA output sharding, so it changes two things.

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (unmodified) and the vLLM fork v0.9.2 release image
scope.checkpoint: K3.25 (vLLM: K3.25-v1; CuteAFD: K3.25-Core-FP8)
scope.items: launcher source, dry-run and capture logs

evidence.text:
- *Omitted differences between the engines' arithmetic or geometry* (found in source and logs, not
  measured):
  - **DSA indexer.** CuteAFD keeps BF16 key/gate rows (`keys`, forced on a head split;
    `dry-run-score.log:1`). vLLM uses FP8 index-K with the B12x kpool top-k (prior audit
    `phase1-indexer-selection.md:31`; `VLLM_USE_B12X_KPOOL_INDEXER=1`). This difference runs in
    CuteAFD's favour for precision. The indexer engages only past about 2K tokens, which is exactly
    where any context-dependent gap would appear. Selection and tie handling differ too (22az).
  - **Attention placement.** CuteAFD uses `context`: MLA split by token across both GPUs, with a
    cross-GPU partial-softmax merge (`dry-run-score.log:61`). vLLM uses `split:25`: whole MLA layers
    owned by one GPU, unsharded (`start.sh:41-45`).
  - **KDA split path.** On CuteAFD, `--kda-output-shard --kda-prefill-expanded` (`run-family.sh:2012-2017`).
  - **Prefill geometry.** vLLM uses 2,045/2,045/262 chunks aligned to 4,352 (`b08.steps.jsonl`), and
    the scored rows straddle chunk boundaries. CuteAFD prefills context in 4,096-row lanes, then scores
    the 512 rows through the scoring path.
  - **Logit precision.** vLLM's logits are BF16 before log-softmax (`logits_dtype: torch.bfloat16` in
    every steps.jsonl). Its head output is rounded too; it is not exact BF16-head arithmetic.
  - **Prefill-shaped scoring measures CuteAFD's W8A8 prefill GEMMs.** Decode and verify rows in serving
    do not use W8A8 activations; prompt KV written during prefill does carry the effect.

- *F1a is confounded.* `GLM5_FLASH_KDA_FP8=off` also removes `--kda-output-shard --kda-prefill-expanded`
  (`run-family.sh:2012-2017`: added only when `kda_fp8 != off`). It reverts to the half-K BF16 partials
  path, whose documented cost is about KL +0.0008 and a top-1 loss (`run-family.sh:1981-1986`). The
  discovery notes this (`discovery-cuteafd-fidelity.md:496`), but `FOLLOWUPS.md:13` describes F1a as a
  pure precision switch. A null or adverse F1a result would be uninterpretable.

findings.question: Do the fidelity set's trailing context rows show a reference-side error, or are they sensitive rows?
findings.statement: All 30 trailing context spans are near-copies of one unrelated filler file; on rows 20 or more positions into a span, cross-engine KL is 0.72, 3.14 and 2.53 nats on three windows (0.008-0.020 on the same windows' generated rows), and vLLM against its own repeat is 1.96 nats on one of them (audit). The audit reads these rows as sensitive to any arithmetic change, not as evidence of a reference-side error.

scope.engine: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (unmodified) and the vLLM fork v0.9.2 release image
scope.checkpoint: K3.25 (vLLM: K3.25-v1; CuteAFD: K3.25-Core-FP8)
scope.items: fidelity set (P-B): trailing context spans

evidence.text:
**U4. Trailing context rows: "a property of the panel's context rows" is right; the implied reference-side cause is not.**
- *All 30 trailing spans are the same filler.* Every span begins `File: rust/crates/cuteafd-api/src/openai/probe.rs`
  (`ctx4.py`). It is an unrelated file inserted as the observation after the model's tool call, for
  example a call to `read_file ledger/dates.py`. The 12,032 rows are 30 near-copies of one text, so they
  are effectively one item. The tokenization is canonical: re-encoding gives identical ids in 30 of 30.
- *The rows are hypersensitive.* Cross-engine KL on rows 20 or more positions into the trailing span
  is 0.72 / 3.14 / 2.53 nats on `a03` / `d03` / `a10` (`ee.py`), against 0.008-0.020 on the same
  windows' gen rows. **vLLM against itself** is 1.96 nats on `a10`, a multi-chunk window. Both engines
  are confident (entropy about 1 nat) but disagree.
- *What follows.* Any arithmetic perturbation produces nat-scale KL on these rows. Both engines being
  about 1.7 nats from the teacher, with NLL below the teacher's, fits "three perturbed copies of a
  fragile computation". It does not show a reference-side error, which A1 (`PROTOCOL-DRAFT.md:162-164`)
  set up as the question.

evidence.text:
**U5. Block L: the code "terminal loop" flags count restated code, not loops** (6 of 8 L3 and 1 of 1 L3s).
- *Evidence* (`l1.py`). Re-tokenizing every L3/L3s code reply:
  - 100% of the repeated 50-grams in the final 4,096-token window have their earlier occurrence in the
    reasoning span.
  - Self-repetition *within* the content is 0.000-0.001.
  - 37-88% of content 50-grams are copied from the reasoning.
  - `exact_period_m08` is `None` for every flagged reply: no periodic structure.
- *What the detector measures here.* The onset sits about 1K tokens before the end of the reasoning
  (for example 42,234 of 43,783). The answer re-states code drafted in the reasoning; this is not looping.
  7 of 8 L3 replies pass all tests (217 tests).

evidence.what: README applies it to both engines
evidence.text: The terminal-loop counts on code replies come from the detector counting the answer restating code drafted in the reasoning; no periodic structure was found in them (audit U5). The code, JSON and prose tasks were sized for thinking off: at the L1 and L2 caps, and for the 1,030-record JSON task at L3, the reasoning leaves too little room for the answer, so those cells measure stop-versus-cap rather than task completion.

evidence.text:
**M1. No drift control or in-run telemetry for Block T.**
- *Run order.* The protocol's CVC drift control (`PROTOCOL-DRAFT.md:19`) has no declared subset. T ran
  V then C (V1 18:35-20:35, C1 22:39-00:29), with no repeat of either.
- *Telemetry.* There is only a pre-run snapshot: temperature, power limit, memory
  (`t/gpu-before-*.txt`: 66/63 °C before V1, 63/61 °C before C1). There are no clocks, power draw or
  throttle reasons during the runs. On 300 W Max-Q cards, 4 hours apart, this is a real gap.
- *A partial CuteAFD repeat exists.* F1-base (`f1/speed-F1-base.json`, same seeds, scoring launch,
  2 hours later) against C1-r1 gives per-cell ratios of 0.96-1.08 on decode and 0.96-1.05 on aggregate.
  So **single-cell noise is about ±4-8%**, and T-SUMMARY ratios between 0.95 and 1.08 cannot be read as
  differences. T-SUMMARY has no intervals, against principle 7 (`PROTOCOL-DRAFT.md:20`).

- **Noise.** A later re-run of CuteAFD (F1-base) shows about ±4-8% per cell; ratios within that range are not
  differences. No drift repeat was run inside Block T; one is declared in FOLLOWUPS.md.

evidence.text:
**Pre-run note (2026-10-28, planner dry runs, before any F1-K4b request).** All five scoring configs fit
(pools: amax/best 1,419,264; kda16 881,152; head16 1,220,096; all16 681,984 tokens). Serving: head16 fits (406,528);
kda16 and all16 do not fit at 262,144 (pool 194,560 short) nor, per the memory rule, at 139,264 (150,016 short):
**serving with BF16 KDA projections does not fit on 2x RTX with K4**. Their precision is still measured (scoring
launches); their speed is not. Speed order becomes base, head16, base.

**Amendment B2 (2026-10-28 13:10, before any further request).** The head16 scoring launch did not fit live either
(KV pool 252,672 tokens, 9,472 short of the 262,144 floor, GPU 0 limiting). B1 is extended to head16's scoring config
(`SPECULATOR=off`), gated by the same nospec control, which now runs first: nospec, head16, kda16, all16. The speed
check is no longer fatal to the run: if the head16 serving launch does not fit live, that is recorded as "does not fit
for serving on 2x RTX with K4" and scoring proceeds.

- **On 2x RTX with K4, only the switches that cost no memory can serve:** W8A16 prefill and the scale rules. BF16 KDA
  and BF16 head do not fit a serving launch here (they would need more GPU memory, e.g. CuteAFD's Spark layouts).
- Speed: not measured for head16/kda16/all16 (serving does not fit); amax/best change stored values only.

evidence.text:
## Design context (added 2026-11-08)
The settings switched off here are the launcher's defaults, with reasons stated by the engine's author. At v4.0.0:
- The launcher comment above the GLM 5.3 Flash precision block (`scripts/launch/run-family.sh:2337-2351`): row128 KDA (FP8,
  one scale per row and 128 input columns) and an FP8 head on both layouts; on the two-GPU head split, token-row KDA output
  ownership, added because it avoids rounding the two GPUs' half-K BF16 partial outputs (its dated check: single-request
  decode +7.6%, paired top-1 453 -> 460 of 512, KL +0.0008).
- The model notes (`docs/models/glm5_flash.md:163-210`, "Default precision"): the trade of single-request decode speed
  (+9.0% on 1 RTX + 2 Sparks) against top-1 and KL on 512 teacher-forced positions, and that the speculation check "does
  not establish byte-identical speculative output".
- The `--kda-fp8` option text (`rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/families/glm5_flash/mod.rs:189-197`): row128 costs top-1 on
  its check and doubles verify-vs-decode rounding, enough to flip greedy output under speculation.
- The model notes and the option text describe BF16 KDA as the default on the two-GPU split; the launcher comment and code
  select row128, which every launch here logged. The documents differ; the launcher's choice is what runs.
The cited checks are teacher-forced on 512 positions; this run measures free generation of long reasoning with speculative
decoding.

Prefill against generation, plain decode against speculative verify, and KDA format against output sharding are not separated (the run's document judges the generation path more likely).

evidence.text:
## Where in the engine (judgement from source and measurements; not isolated by its own run, added 2026-11-08)
Judged most likely on the generation path (decode and speculative verify); prefill is not excluded.
- Prompts are 1,155-1,758 tokens; median reasoning is 50-68K tokens per arm, so prefill is about 2-3% of the tokens.
- Speculative verify steps run on the decode programs (`engine.rs:4660`, `:4686`: "speculative steps are
  decode-shaped"); with FP8 KDA, decode rows read the FP8 copies and KDA output sharding is not limited to prefill
  (`engine.rs:3844-3847`, `:4666-4695`).
- Not excluded: the KDA setting also changes the KDA projections in prefill, and the recurrent state the prompt leaves
  seeds every later token. The prefill-activation switch (F-pre) covers the MLA and MLP activations only, not the KDA
  projections (the launcher's default list is mla,ffn), so it does not bear on this.
- FP8 MLA projections (MLA q_b and o_proj included) run on decode rows in every F arm and the gap still closes.
- Teacher-forced results elsewhere in this investigation (stop decision, KL) run through the prefill programs on
  science-question traces; they do not measure this path on code.
Open: KDA in prefill against generation; plain decode against speculative verify (with FP8 KDA, decode rows up to 64 take
the FP8 GEMV and wider verify steps W8A16); KDA format against output sharding.

findings.statement: By the launch logs and the v4.0.0 source: the BF16-core arm (and K4) runs the KDA projections in row128 FP8 (with the f_a, g_a and b projections packed into the FP8 operand), an FP8 vocabulary head and FP8 prefill activations for MLA and FFN, while the native 6-bit arm runs KDA and the head on its 6-bit kernels without activation quantization. MLA, dense and shared-expert projections are FP8 on the BF16 path, with no BF16 option on v4.

evidence.text:
## Server logs (read)
| Launch | KDA projections | Vocabulary head | Prefill FP8 activations |
|---|---|---|---|
| K4-Core-K6, native 6-bit core (C-K6) | `kda_fp8=Off` (native 6-bit) | `head="K6"`, `fp8_head=false` | `fp8_prefill=[Mla, Ffn]` (no FP8 MLA/FFN operands to apply it to) |
| K4-Core-K6, BF16 core (C-K6x) | `kda_fp8=Row128`, 2,844 MiB | `head="FP8"`, `fp8_head=true` | `fp8_prefill=[Mla, Ffn]` |
| K4 (C-K4) | `kda_fp8=Row128`, 2,844 MiB | `head="FP8"`, `fp8_head=true` | `fp8_prefill=[Mla, Ffn]` |
Source: `results/2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap` server logs, s1 launches (not published; lines 75-80 of each).
The two serving configs differ only in MODEL_ID and MODEL_REVISION.

## Code (read)
- MLA (`q_a|kv_a`, `q_b`, `o_proj`), dense and shared-expert projections are FP8 only: the checkpoint's E4M3 blocks, or
  128x128 blocks quantized from BF16 at load; BF16 is never resident (`rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/families/glm5_flash/weights.rs:3-10`).
- KDA in/out projections and the LM head take FP8 (E4M3, per row x 128-K scales) when selected
  (`weights.rs:3-10`). The launcher's `auto` selects both: `GLM5_FLASH_KDA_FP8` auto -> row128
  (`scripts/launch/run-family.sh:2355-2363`), `GLM5_FLASH_FP8_HEAD` auto -> on (`run-family.sh:2409-2417`).
- With a native 6-bit core the daemon turns KDA FP8 off and, with a native `lm_head`, the FP8 head off
  (`rust/crates/cuteafd-daemon/src/families/glm5_flash/mod.rs:1716-1723`). So the BF16-core checkpoint gets FP8 KDA and an
  FP8 head; the 6-bit checkpoint does not.
- The KDA FP8 input operand packs q, k, v and the f_a, g_a and b projections; f_a/g_a/b are BF16 in both checkpoints and stay
  BF16 on the 6-bit path (`weights.rs:731-746`, native: separate BF16 `w_aux`; loader
  `rust/crates/cuteafd-loader/src/families/glm5_flash/resident.rs:94-104`, converted: one input operand, 1 byte per value with FP8).
- The option's own documentation: row128 "costs 3.4 points top-1 (89.1% -> 85.7%) and doubles verify-vs-decode rounding
  ... enough to flip greedy output under speculation; opt-in", CLI default off (`mod.rs:189-198`).
- Scale rule for FP8 copies made at load: default pow2 (smallest power of two >= amax/448) (`mod.rs:284-294`).
- Prefill: MLA and FFN run W8A8 (dynamic FP8 activations) by default (`GLM5_FLASH_FP8_PREFILL`, `run-family.sh:2446-2465`);
  on the 6-bit path these operands are 6-bit trellis kernels (FP16 weights, FP32 accumulate) with no activation quantization.

## Switches that exist on v4 (read)
`GLM5_FLASH_KDA_FP8=off` (BF16 KDA), `GLM5_FLASH_FP8_HEAD=off` (BF16 head), `GLM5_FLASH_FP8_PREFILL=off`, `FP8_SCALES`.
MLA and dense/shared MLP have no BF16 option.

findings.question: On CuteAFD v4.0.0 on two GPUs, does switching KDA FP8 off change anything besides the KDA projections' format?
findings.statement: On the two-GPU head split the launcher's default also adds KDA output sharding (token-row output ownership) unless KDA FP8 is off; the daemon accepts it only with FP8 KDA and clears it for a native 6-bit core. Switching KDA FP8 off on two GPUs therefore also returns KDA to the partials split path.

- Added 2026-11-07: on a two-GPU head split the launcher's `auto` also adds token-row KDA output ownership
  (`--kda-output-shard --kda-prefill-expanded`) unless KDA FP8 is off (`run-family.sh:2366`); the daemon accepts these

findings.question: What reasons does CuteAFD v4.0.0's own documentation give for these launch defaults, and do its documents agree?
findings.statement: The settings are the launcher's defaults, with reasons in its comment: row128 KDA and an FP8 head on both layouts, and on the two-GPU split token-row KDA output ownership to avoid rounding the two GPUs' half-K BF16 partials; the model notes give the speed trade with teacher-forced checks (top-1, KL). The model notes and the --kda-fp8 option text describe BF16 KDA as the two-GPU default, so the documents differ, and the launcher's choice is what runs.

evidence.text:
Design context (added 2026-11-08): these settings are the launcher's defaults, with its stated reasons in the comment above
the GLM 5.3 Flash precision block (`scripts/launch/run-family.sh:2337-2351`): row128 KDA and an FP8 head on both layouts,
token-row KDA output ownership on the two-GPU head split because it avoids rounding half-K BF16 partials. The model
notes (`docs/models/glm5_flash.md:163-210`, "Default precision") give the speed trade and its teacher-forced checks (top-1,
KL); they and the `--kda-fp8` option text (`.../glm5_flash/mod.rs:189-197`, which also records the verify-vs-decode
rounding cost under speculation) describe BF16 KDA as the default on the two-GPU split. The documents differ; the
launcher's choice is what runs. This note maps what each setting changes.

findings.replication: within one launch only; launch-to-launch repeatability is CP's bf16_distance repeat

evidence.text:
- **Loads.** `hqa` ready in about 60 s, pool 2,097,152 tokens, 94.2 / 93.2 GiB used. `anchor` ready in about
  80 s, pool 1,318,400 tokens, BF16 head, no FP8. Other arms are first launched by step A.
- **Row alignment.** From the dumps, row p holds the distribution that selects `ids[p]`: mean log-probability at
  shift 0 is −5.1 (decode path) / −4.6 (prefill path), against −11.6 to −14.9 at shifts ±1 and ±2. Rows are
  normalised.
- **Determinism within a launch.** Decode-path capture twice: 64 of 64 rows hash-equal. Cold prefill twice at
  22K: 32 of 32 rows hash-equal.
- **Reply round trip.** `generated` ends with the stop token (`<|user|>`, 154827); the next turn's rendered prompt

syntheses.question: Where does most of a configuration's distance from the BF16 model come from: the routed experts, the core, or the engine?
syntheses.judgement: From the routed experts. On CuteAFD v4.0.0 the step from 3.25-bit to 4-bit experts (K3.25 to K4) changed teacher-panel KL by −0.0195. On the same checkpoint the engine changed it by +0.0017 (K3.25) and +0.0035 (K4). The core moved it less: on the fidelity set hqa was 0.0026 closer than the BF16 core, and on the teacher panel the BF16-core configuration was not the closest (anchor 0.0320, compact 0.0297, intervals overlapping). In the v5 study K3.25-Core-FP8 was farther than every 4-bit-expert configuration on both sets, by +0.0124 to +0.0183 on the fidelity set.
syntheses.strength_basis: Comparisons planned before their data, on two reference sets (teacher panel, fidelity set) and two engines, point the same way. The expert step is resolved on the teacher panel in the v4 run. The whole-checkpoint step is resolved on both sets in the v5 run (20 of 20 intervals exclude 0). The top-20 ratios agree in direction on both engines and both panels. Engine and core differences are resolved or bounded, and each is under a fifth of the expert step.
syntheses.scope: GLM-5.3-Flash on two RTX PRO 6000; prefill path; contexts to 14.4K; CuteAFD v3.0.1, v4.0.0 and v5.0.0 and the vLLM fork v0.9.2.

syntheses.question: Why does CuteAFD's BF16-core arm think shorter on code than its native 6-bit-core arm?
syntheses.judgement: Most of the gap goes with CuteAFD's FP8 KDA setting. The native 6-bit core thought 1.26 [1.24, 1.29] times as long as the BF16 core run through the engine's FP8 defaults, on 12 new code prompts. Switching the KDA setting off lengthened the BF16-core arm 1.31 [1.24, 1.38] times; turning the head and prefill FP8 off after that added nothing detectable. On the vLLM fork, which runs neither core through these FP8 paths, the two cores thought equally long: 1.00 [0.96, 1.04]. The setting changes both the KDA projection format and, on two GPUs, KDA output sharding, and the run does not separate the two.
syntheses.short: Mostly CuteAFD's FP8 KDA setting: switching it off lengthened code thinking 1.31x, about the whole gap; on the vLLM fork the two cores think alike (1.00 [0.96, 1.04]).
syntheses.strength_basis: Frozen protocols, one prompt family (16 code prompts, 12 primary) and one checkpoint pair; the engine contrast and the setting ablation point the same way.
syntheses.scope: GLM-5.3-Flash on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (300 W); CuteAFD v4.0.0 and vLLM fork v0.9.2 with the local core loader; K4-Core-K6 and its BF16-core derivative; code prompts, thinking on.

syntheses.question: Does shorter thinking cost correctness on code?
syntheses.judgement: Not settled. The 1.26x length gap between CuteAFD's two arms came with no detected difference in all-tests-pass: +1.6 points [−7.8, +10.9]. But in a post hoc look the arm with every FP8 path off passed more often than either CuteAFD arm (+17.5 points [+7.8, +28.6] against the BF16-core default), which also holds after a correction for 13 looks; that arm ran a day later on the same prompt family.
syntheses.short: Not settled: the 1.26x length gap came with no detected pass-rate difference (+1.6 points [−7.8, +10.9]), but an all-BF16-path arm passed more often in a post hoc look.
syntheses.strength_basis: One pre-set comparison not detected, one post hoc comparison resolved; mixed.

syntheses.question: What does turning CuteAFD's FP8 settings off cost in speed and memory?
syntheses.judgement: W8A16 prefill costs about 4% in time to first token in every cell measured (1.038 to 1.045 on K3.25) with decode within run-to-run noise, and fits every launch measured. BF16 KDA projections and a BF16 head shrink the KV pool: on K4-Core-K6 (v4.0.0) from 1,931,264 tokens to 1,414,656 (KDA) and 1,215,488 (KDA and head). On K4 with v3.0.1, a serving launch with BF16 KDA did not fit; with a BF16 head the planner's dry run fit, and a live launch fell 9,472 tokens short of the context floor. Decode with BF16 KDA was 0.92 of as shipped on K3.25.
syntheses.short: W8A16 prefill: about 4% first-token time; BF16 KDA and head: a smaller KV pool (1,931,264 to 1,215,488 tokens on K4-Core-K6), and BF16 KDA did not fit a K4 serving launch on v3.0.1.
syntheses.strength_basis: Measured in follow-ups on three runs and three checkpoints with consistent direction; speed is descriptive against each run's noise band.
syntheses.scope: GLM-5.3-Flash on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (300 W); CuteAFD v3.0.1 and v4.0.0; K3.25, K4, K4-Core-K6.

syntheses.question: Is CuteAFD faster than the vLLM fork on this machine?
syntheses.judgement: On v4.0.0, faster or level in every cell measured on K3.25 and K4 (aggregate faster in 19 and 22 of 22 cells, slower in none), and K4-Core-K6 on CuteAFD was faster or level against the vLLM fork running K4 (20 of 22 faster); time to first token at 128K 19.8 s against 34.9 s on K3.25. On v3.0.1 CuteAFD was faster in single-stream decode (1.02 to 1.41) and in aggregate at 32K-128K, but slower in aggregate at 1K input with 8 streams (0.87 to 0.93), in first token at 1K (0.40-0.41 s against 0.25-0.26 s) and in first token at 32K-128K with 4-16 streams (1.18-1.47).

syntheses.question: How much context fits, and how long does a start take?
syntheses.judgement: CuteAFD v4.0.0 holds a larger KV pool than the vLLM fork on the same checkpoint: 5,799,424 against 4,762,898 tokens on K3.25 and 1,931,264 against 1,377,179 on K4. It is ready in 81-91 s; the vLLM fork in 257-349 s with its JIT caches kept between starts, and 697 s without them. On v3.0.1, CuteAFD needed MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=262144 to start K4 on two GPUs.
syntheses.short: CuteAFD v4.0.0: larger KV pools (1,931,264 vs 1,377,179 tokens on K4) and ready in 81-91 s against 257-349 s.
syntheses.strength_basis: Recorded on every launch of several runs; the direction is the same in each. Start times are one or two starts per configuration.

syntheses.question: Does the same request give the same result twice?
syntheses.judgement: On CuteAFD, yes: scoring rows were bit-identical between passes, launches, days and releases (93,670 of 93,670 rows across launches; 18,286 of 18,286 across days), and tool-calling statuses were the same in all three repeats. On the vLLM fork, rows inside the first 2,045-token prefill chunk repeat exactly and rows beyond it almost never do, and tool-calling status changed between repeats on 8 of 88 scenarios.
syntheses.short: CuteAFD: bit-identical across launches, days and releases. vLLM fork: varies beyond its first prefill chunk.
syntheses.strength_basis: Checked in five runs on each engine, with the same result each time.
